title: Tortellini with Butternut, Broccoli & Red Lentils
source: Built for Jarred's kids - no cheese

2 servings: 1/4 cup dried RED lentils, rinsed (not green or brown - see notes)
1/4 small onion, chopped, or 1 clove garlic
1 tsp white (shiro) miso - or just 1/2 tsp salt
Salt, and a small squeeze of lemon at the end
4 servings: 1/2 cup dried RED lentils, rinsed (not green or brown - see notes)
1/2 small onion, chopped, or 2 cloves garlic
2 tsp white (shiro) miso - or just 1 tsp salt
Salt, and a squeeze of lemon at the end

steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the squash with the olive oil and a good pinch of salt and spread it in a single layer on a sheet pan - crowded squash steams instead of browning. Roast 25-30 min, until the edges are genuinely caramelized. Add the chopped onion to the pan for the last 15 min. (2/3-inch cubes run faster: 20-25 min, check at 18.)
Meanwhile, put the red lentils and the stock in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 min, until the lentils have collapsed completely and the whole thing looks like a loose puree.

Add the broccoli to the lentil pan for the LAST 4-5 minutes only, just until a knife goes through. Longer and it goes army green and starts tasting like broccoli - which is the thing you are trying to avoid.
Boil the tortellini from frozen while the squash finishes. RESERVE 1 CUP of the pasta water before draining.

Blend the roasted squash and onion with the lentils, broccoli and all their liquid, plus the butter, miso and nutmeg, until completely smooth - 45 seconds, longer than feels necessary. Any texture left is what a kid will find.
Taste and salt properly, then add a small squeeze of lemon - it lifts the whole thing out of flat-and-sweet.
Toss with the drained tortellini over low heat for a minute, thinning with the reserved pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce coats rather than clumps.
notes: NO CHEESE, ON PURPOSE - and it does not need it. Cheese in a sauce like this is doing four jobs: salt, fat, umami and body. Here the lentils give the body, the butter gives the fat, the miso gives the umami, and you salt it properly at the end. That is the whole swap. IF YOU WANT MORE OF THAT SAVOURY EDGE without dairy: 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast tastes genuinely cheesy; 1 Tbsp tahini or cashew butter adds the richness Parmesan was carrying; a teaspoon of soy sauce works in place of the miso. RED LENTILS ONLY. Red (or yellow) lentils have no skins, so they fall apart completely in 15 min and vanish into the sauce. Green, brown or French lentils hold their shape no matter how long you cook them - a kid will spot them and the texture is grainy. This matters more than any other choice in the recipe. ROAST THE SQUASH, DO NOT BOIL IT. Boiled squash tastes like baby food - watery and flat. The caramelized edges are where all the sweetness comes from, and the sweetness is the whole reason kids eat this. In a hurry, microwave it covered with 2 Tbsp water for 8 min and stir in 1 tsp of honey to make up for what you lost. ROASTING TIME IS ABOUT PIECE SIZE, NOT QUANTITY - a third of a cup and three cups take the same time. 1-inch cubes 25-30 min at 425F, 2/3-inch cubes 20-25 min, flip once around the 15-minute mark. For a small amount use a small pan or a toaster oven; a few cubes on a big hot sheet pan scorch at the edges before the centres soften. FOR A YOUNG KID, cook past fork-tender to genuinely mashable - it should squash with light pressure between your fingers. Firm cubes are a choking risk and a toddler rejects a texture before she ever gets to the flavour. BROCCOLI GOES IN LAST. Four to five minutes, no more. Overcooked broccoli turns the sauce a muddy olive colour and brings a sulphur smell that is exactly what gets a plate pushed away. WHAT ELSE CAN GO IN: roasted carrot or sweet potato (more sweetness, same colour); cauliflower (disappears completely); a peeled roasted red pepper (deeper, slightly smoky); white beans or a spoon of red lentils more for extra protein; a pinch of smoked paprika for the adults' bowls. Spinach or peas work but turn the sauce green instead of orange - fine if your kids do not care about colour, a dealbreaker if they do. PASTA WATER, NOT MORE STOCK, for thinning. The starch is what makes it cling to the tortellini instead of sliding off into a puddle. FOR THE ADULTS: brown a tablespoon of butter with a few sage leaves and spoon it over the top, plus black pepper and chilli flakes. FREEZES WELL - the sauce on its own, not with the pasta in it. Roast a whole bag of squash, make a double batch of sauce and freeze half in a jar; it is a 10-minute dinner later. Thin with water when reheating, it sets up thick in the fridge.

title: Broccoli, Butternut Squash & Lentils (No Cheese)
servings: about 6 kid portions (batch cooks and freezes)
source: Variation on Tiny Tums Recipes (@tinytumsrecipes), de-cheesed
ingredients: 150 g dry brown lentils (3/4 cup) - or red lentils, see notes
600 ml low-salt chicken or vegetable stock (about 2 1/2 cups)
1 cup butternut squash, peeled and finely grated (or diced very small)
1 cup broccoli florets, chopped very fine (pea-sized)
1 Tbsp butter or olive oil, stirred in at the end - this replaces the fat the cheese was bringing
OPTIONAL, for the savoury edge: 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast, or 1 tsp white (shiro) miso, or 1 Tbsp tahini
PICK ONE OR TWO ADD-INS, about 1 cup total - see the notes for when each goes in: grated carrot; finely diced sweet potato; finely chopped cauliflower; 1 jarred roasted red pepper, chopped
steps: Rinse the lentils and pick out any small stones or shriveled lentils.

Heat the oil in a pot over medium. Add the garlic and squash and saute 3-4 min, until the squash softens and the garlic is fragrant. GRATED CARROT and DICED SWEET POTATO go in here too, with the squash.
Add the lentils and all the stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer 18-20 min.

Add the broccoli and simmer 8-10 min more, stirring now and then, until the lentils and broccoli are very soft (25-30 min total for the lentils). CAULIFLOWER goes in here, with the broccoli. Add a splash of water if it dries out.

Take it off the heat. Stir in the butter, and the nutritional yeast, miso or tahini if using. CHOPPED ROASTED RED PEPPER goes in now, off the heat - it is already cooked and simmering it just turns it to mush.
Mash with a fork to the texture she likes, loose or smooth. Taste it yourself before serving.
notes: NO CHEESE. The cheddar was doing four jobs and each has a replacement: FAT - the tablespoon of butter or oil stirred in off the heat, which is what keeps it from tasting lean and watery. UMAMI - 1 tsp white miso or 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast; nutritional yeast is the closest single swap to a cheesy flavour and has no salt, which matters under 2. BODY - the lentils already do this, which is why this recipe misses the cheese far less than the orzo version does. SALT - for an older kid or an adult bowl, salt it properly at the end; most 'tastes flat without cheese' is actually under-salting. Miso and tahini both bring salt, so for under 1 use the nutritional yeast or neither. WHEN EACH ADD-IN GOES IN, this is the part that matters: GRATED CARROT and FINELY DICED SWEET POTATO go in at the start with the squash - they need the full cook and both add sweetness and keep the orange colour. FINELY CHOPPED CAULIFLOWER goes in with the broccoli for the last 8-10 min; it disappears completely into the mash and is the most invisible vegetable here. JARRED ROASTED RED PEPPER goes in at the very end, off the heat - it is already cooked, it only needs to warm through, and simmering it turns it to slurry. It brings a deeper, slightly smoky sweetness and is the biggest flavour change of the four. Stick to about 1 cup of add-ins total or you throw off the lentil-to-liquid ratio and it goes soupy; add a splash more stock if you go heavier. AVOID SPINACH AND PEAS here unless you do not mind the colour - they turn the whole thing muddy green instead of orange. LENTILS: brown lentils hold a little shape, which is fine if you are mashing. Red lentils collapse completely in about 15 min and give a smoother, more sauce-like result - cut the stock to about 500 ml and the simmer to 15 min if you use them. MASHABLE SOFT is the bar for a toddler, not fork-tender - the lentils, broccoli and squash should all squash with light pressure. Lentils are high in fibre, so start with smaller portions. The squash is sauteed first for flavour and melts into the lentils; the broccoli goes in last so it stays green and does not turn sulfury. Pre-cut squash saves the peeling. FREEZE single portions in ice-cube trays and reheat with a splash of water.
